[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Docker for Python Developers: Containers, Images, and Dockerfiles"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a practical introduction to Docker for Python developers. We'll cover the core concepts of containers, images, and Dockerfiles, demonstrating how to use them to package and deploy Python applications."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is Docker?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Docker is a platform for developing, shipping, and running applications in isolated environments called containers. Containers package up an application and all its dependencies, ensuring that it runs reliably across different computing environments. Docker uses images as blueprints for creating containers."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Concepts"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"**Containers:** Isolated environments that run applications. They share the host OS kernel but have their own file system, processes, and network interfaces."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"**Images:** Read-only templates used to create containers. An image contains the application code, libraries, and dependencies needed to run the application."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"**Dockerfiles:** Text files that contain instructions for building Docker images. They specify the base image, dependencies to install, and commands to execute."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Docker installed on your system (https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic knowledge of Python"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Simple Python Application"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let's start with a basic Python application. Create a file named `app.py` with the following content:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"python
from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/')
def hello_world():
    return 'Hello, Docker!'

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(debug=True, host='0.0.0.0')
"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"This is a simple Flask application that displays "Hello, Docker!" in the browser."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Dockerfile"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, let's create a `Dockerfile` in the same directory as `app.py`:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"dockerfile
FROM python:3.9-slim-buster

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt . 
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY app.py .

EXPOSE 5000

CMD ["python", "app.py"]
"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Explanation of the Dockerfile instructions:"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`FROM python:3.9-slim-buster`: Specifies the base image to use (Python 3.9 slim version)."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`WORKDIR /app`: Sets the working directory inside the container."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`COPY requirements.txt .`: Copies the `requirements.txt` file (if it exists) to the working directory."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt`: Installs the Python dependencies specified in `requirements.txt`."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`COPY app.py .`: Copies the `app.py` file to the working directory."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`EXPOSE 5000`: Exposes port 5000 to allow access to the application."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`CMD ["python", "app.py"]`: Specifies the command to run when the container starts."},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a `requirements.txt` file with the following content:"},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"
Flask
"},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Building the Docker Image"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Open your terminal and navigate to the directory containing the `Dockerfile` and `app.py`. Run the following command to build the Docker image:"},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"bash
docker build -t my-python-app .
"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command builds an image named `my-python-app` using the `Dockerfile` in the current directory (`.`)."},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Running the Docker Container"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"After the image is built, you can run a container from it using the following command:"},{"order":35,"type":"code","text":"bash
docker run -d -p 5000:5000 my-python-app
"},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"Explanation of the command:"},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`-d`: Runs the container in detached mode (in the background)."},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`-p 5000:5000`: Maps port 5000 on the host machine to port 5000 in the container."},{"order":39,"type":"paragraph","text":"Open your web browser and navigate to `http://localhost:5000`. You should see "Hello, Docker!" displayed."},{"order":40,"type":"subheading","text":"Stopping and Removing the Container"},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"To stop the container, first find its ID using `docker ps`:"},{"order":42,"type":"code","text":"bash
docker ps
"},{"order":43,"type":"paragraph","text":"Then, stop the container using its ID:"},{"order":44,"type":"code","text":"bash
docker stop <container_id>
"},{"order":45,"type":"paragraph","text":"To remove the container:"},{"order":46,"type":"code","text":"bash
docker rm <container_id>
"},{"order":47,"type":"paragraph","text":"To remove the image:"},{"order":48,"type":"code","text":"bash
docker rmi my-python-app
"},{"order":49,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":50,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provided a basic introduction to Docker for Python developers. You learned how to create Dockerfiles, build images, and run containers. Docker simplifies the process of packaging and deploying Python applications, ensuring consistency across different environments."}]
